title: Kiehl finiteness for relatively pseudo-coherent complexes
statement: Let $h:Z\to T$ be a proper morphism of arbitrary schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $E\in D(\mathcal O_Z)$ [def-pc-derived-category]. Suppose that $E$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $T$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Then $Rh_*E$ [def-pc-derived-direct-image] is pseudo-coherent on $T$ [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Neither flatness nor local finite presentation of $h$ is assumed; there is no Noetherian or global quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness assumption on $Z,T$, and no global lower cohomological bound on $E$.

source.place: Tag 0CSD, lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general: unnumbered paragraph immediately after the lemma statement, beginning "More generally", citing Kiehl. This is the general relative assertion in that paragraph, not the flat lemma itself.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset T$, put $X=h^{-1}V$, $f=h|_X$, and $F=E|_X$. The definition of properness gives that $f$ is separated and finite type; its universal-closedness tests are a subset of the tests for $h$, so $f$ is proper. By the all-affine-charts criterion, the relative pseudo-coherence tests for $F$ over $V$ are among those for $E$ over $T$, for every integer $m$. Thus $F$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $V$. Open restriction of derived direct image identifies $(Rh_*E)|_V$ with $Rf_*F$. It is enough to prove pseudo-coherence of this object for every $V$, since the conclusion is local by its definition.

source.place: Tag 0CSD, unnumbered general assertion following lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; agent assembly

proof.text: Set $C=R\Gamma(X,F)$. The finite-degree Noetherian approximation lemma gives that $F$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Since $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (finite type and separated), $Rf_*F$ has quasi-coherent cohomology. Computing $Rf_*F$ by a K-injective resolution $I$ of $F$, the global-sections acyclicity of $f_*I$ (with $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_A$) gives $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A,Rf_*F)\cong\Gamma(X,I)=C$ in $D(A)$. The affine derived equivalence therefore identifies $Rf_*F$ with $\widetilde C$. For each integer $m$, apply the approximation lemma with $n=m$. It supplies $A_0$, a proper $f_0:X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}A_0$, bounded coherent $F_0$, and $\alpha:A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_0}C_0\to C$, where $C_0=R\Gamma(X_0,F_0)$; $H^i(\alpha)$ is an isomorphism for $i>m$ and is surjective for $i=m$. Properness is used here only to choose $f_0$ proper.

source.place: Tag 0CSD, unnumbered general assertion following lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; agent assembly

proof.text: The ring $A_0$ is Noetherian, and $f_0$ is proper. Apply the Noetherian proper bounded-coherent-image theorem to $F_0$. It gives bounded coherent cohomology for $Rf_{0*}F_0$. This object is pseudo-coherent by the Noetherian bounded-coherent criterion. By the same global-sections acyclicity for $f_{0*}$ of a K-injective resolution of $F_0$, $R\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A_0,Rf_{0*}F_0)\cong C_0$ in $D(A_0)$, so under the affine derived equivalence it corresponds to $C_0$. The affine pseudo-coherence criterion therefore gives a bounded-above finite free $A_0$-complex $P_0^\bullet$ representing $C_0$. No flatness or finite Tor dimension of $f_0$ or $F_0$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0CSD, unnumbered general assertion following lemma-flat-proper-pseudo-coherent-direct-image-general; agent assembly

proof.text: The bounded-above finite free complex $P_0^\bullet$ is termwise flat and hence K-flat by the bounded-above flat K-flat lemma. Consequently $P^\bullet=A\otimes_{A_0}P_0^\bullet$ represents $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_0}C_0$. Its term in degree $i$ is finite free over $A$, of exactly the rank of $P_0^i$, and it vanishes above the same bound. This is a computation on the chosen resolution, so no flatness of $A$ over $A_0$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 0650, lemma-pull-pseudo-coherent: compute on a bounded-above finite free model

proof.text: Let $Q^\bullet=\sigma_{\ge m}P^\bullet$ be the stupid truncation, with terms $P^i$ for $i\ge m$ and zero terms below $m$. It is bounded finite free and has its evident map $Q^\bullet\to P^\bullet$. In degrees $i>m$, boundaries and cycles are unchanged, so this map induces isomorphisms on cohomology. In degree $m$, it induces the quotient map $\ker d^m\to\ker d^m/\operatorname{im}d^{m-1}$, hence a surjection. Compose with the isomorphism to $A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A_0}C_0$ and with $\alpha$. The resulting $Q^\bullet\to C$ is an isomorphism on cohomology above $m$ and a surjection in degree $m$. This is precisely $m$-pseudo-coherence of $C$.

source.place: Tag 064Q, definition-pseudo-coherent: explicit finite free approximation

proof.text: The integer $m$ was arbitrary, so $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent for every $m$. The all-$m$ criterion makes $C$ pseudo-coherent. The affine pseudo-coherence criterion then makes $\widetilde C\simeq Rf_*F$ pseudo-coherent. This holds on every affine open $V$ in Step 1; the local definition gives that $Rh_*E$ is pseudo-coherent on $T$. The argument chooses its bounds and approximation data separately on each $V$ and for each $m$, and therefore needs no global quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or lower cohomological bound.
